newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency to review potato imports from Canada.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency to review potato imports from Canada.

text.p: The U.S. International Trade Commission announced Thursday it would review factors in U.S. and Canadian potato production, including trends in Canadian shipments to the U.S. market.
The fact-finding study was undertaken at the request of U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky's office and would cover the period 1992-96.

Meanwhile, Senator Byron Dorgan urged Barshefsky to initiate consultations with Canada over an upturn in wheat exports. Dorgan, North Dakota Democrat, said the current pace of imports suggested Canada would "bump" against an informal U.S.-set threshhold of 50 million bushels per marketing year.

"When we have a significant trade deficit with Canada, it doesn't make any sense to me to have continuing grain imports from Canada," Dorgan said in a statement. "I expect and I hope the administration will take some action on this."

U.S. growers have complained for years of unfair competition from Canada on a wide range of field and livestock products. The United States recently lost a challenge before a North American Free Trade Agreement tribunal of Canada's restrictions on dairy and livestock trade.

The two nations, who are each other's largest trade partner, agreed to a limit on Canadian wheat shipments earlier this decade. The agreement has expired but the United States has said it would stand by the limits unilaterally.
Dorgan said wheat consultations would be a warning to Canada to constrain its wheat exports.
The U.S. Agriculture Department has forecast the United States would import 75 million bushels of wheat this marketing year, compared to 68 million bushels in 1995/96.
